MatMech · paper → logical graph

MatMech argument graphs

Each paper becomes one directed graph that follows its argument: hypothesis → selection → processing → structure → property → performance → discussion. Measurements sit in between as evidence nodes, and each figure-to-claim edge names the multimodal reasoning step it performs. Node types come from a shared vocabulary built by a saturation sweep: staff agents decomposed papers and a senior-investigator agent ruled on every new type.

The ten stages as one graph

Every node in every paper belongs to one of ten first-level stages. Arrows are the actual edges between stages, summed over all 60 papers (2,625 edges). Arrow width is proportional to the count, and circle area to the number of nodes. The spine runs left to right. Mechanism bridges it from above, and observations and prior knowledge feed it from below. Loops within a stage are shown as ↻ counts. Hover an arrow for its relation types.

Saturation

Vocabulary

Types name the role a node plays in the argument. Materials, techniques, values and directions go in attributes. Click a stage to expand it.

Multimodal reasoning operations

These are the verbs on figure → claim edges: what a reader does to the image to get the claim.

Relations

Cases

Solid, thicker outlines mark the spine (the main argument). Teal edges carry a multimodal operation. Dashed red outlines are image-audit nodes, where the figure contradicts or adds to the text. Select a node for its definition, attributes and figure.
